text:
maria_sales: Quick netops handoff for Acme POC. They want TLS inspection but also need original client IP in app logs for auditing. Options? PrivateLink, peering, or an inline proxy? cc @sam_se @jon_netops @priya_acme

sam_se: TL;DR: PrivateLink or VPC peering preserve source IP if you do TCP passthrough. Terminating proxies or NAT will replace it. If they must terminate TLS for inspection, use PROXY protocol or X-Forwarded-For chain.

jon_netops: A few practical constraints to call out:
- NLB in TCP mode + PrivateLink -> preserves client source IP and works with PROXY protocol v1/v2 if enabled.
- ALB (HTTP/HTTPS) terminates TLS and the backend sees the ALB IP unless you use X-Forwarded-For headers. ALB won't preserve raw src IP at TCP layer.
- VPC peering = direct L3 connectivity, preserves IPs, but requires route table & security group changes on both sides.

priya_acme: They have strict firewall rules and only allow specific egress IPs. Can we offer static egress from Redwood side?

maria_sales: Short answer: we can allocate a fixed EIP on our egress/NAT for the POC or recommend PrivateLink so traffic does not traverse public internet. @alex_finance will provide the pricing line.

alex_finance: Pricing guidance for the quote: PrivateLink endpoint charge (region dependent) + AWS Data Processing per GB (~$0.01-$0.09/GB) + our Private deployment egress line item if we route via our NAT/EIP. For a rough POC estimate, include an endpoint setup fee on the SOW. I'll add a note to the quote.

amanda_security: From sec questionnaire POV: PrivateLink reduces attack surface and is preferred. For audit logs: we support customer-managed KMS, and can forward audit logs to their SIEM over a secure log-forwarder. If they use TLS-inspect proxies that add/strip headers, confirm log integrity controls.

jon_netops: Practical firewall snippet they can hand to their ops team:
```
# Allow outbound to PrivateLink endpoint ENIs (recommended)
Egress: TCP 443 -> vpce-xxxxxxxx (PrivateLink ENI IPs)
# OR if peering to our VPC
Egress: TCP 443 -> 10.20.30.0/24 (our peer subnet)
# If using fixed EIP (we'll allocate)
Egress: TCP 443 -> 52.23.45.67/32
```

jon_netops: Runbook notes:
- If proxy terminates TLS, enable PROXY protocol on NLB and ensure backend/proxy is configured to emit/consume PROXY headers. We support v1 and v2.
- If customer uses inline TLS inspection but preserves TCP passthrough (SNI routing only), client IP stays intact.
- Health check: NLB health checks expect TCP on the service port. Open that on their firewall for the health check source ranges.

sam_se: Ops caveat: enabling PROXY protocol adds a header to the TCP stream. Some older proxies may not handle v2; confirm compatibility. We'll add both options to the runbook and prefer v2 if they need binary-safe fields.

maria_sales: Priya, can you confirm whether Acme's TLS inspection appliance supports PROXY protocol v1/v2 or will they need X-Forwarded-For?

priya_acme: I'll check with our NetOps (we use F5 and a cloud proxy). F5 supports PROXY v1/v2 on passthrough configs. We'll confirm exact model/firmware.

deploybot: ticket NET-PROC-903 created: allocate vpce, optional EIP, enable PROXY protocol flag, tag with customer:acme-poc.

alex_finance: I'll attach a provisional cost line to the POC quote and mark private connectivity as a billable optional.

maria_sales: Great. Action items for POC runbook: 1) Confirm proxy PROXY protocol support (Priya). 2) Decide PrivateLink vs peering (Acme). 3) Finance to provide estimate (Alex). 4) Infra to provision endpoint + tag (NET-PROC-903). I'll update the POC doc and circle back. :thumbsup:
